classification.difficultyReason: Interpret the supplied graphs; in part (b), use the vertical chord midpoint to infer the centre, calculate the radius, then substitute axis conditions to find all intercepts.

content.prompt: Write down the equations of the following circles, and state any intercepts with the coordinate axes.

spec.description: Equal-scale coordinate axes, supplied blue circle and centre point, dashed centre guides, x ticks 3 and 6, and y tick 4. No grid or origin label. Source graph blue is normalised to the standard series blue.
spec.mathematics: Circle centre (3,4), radius 3, tangent to the y-axis at (0,4).
spec.answerVisibility: All source givens visible; no equation, radius value or added intercept labels appear in the student figure.

answer.worked:
The centre is $(3,4)$ and the radius is $3$.
$$\begin{align*}(x-3)^2+(y-4)^2&=3^2\\(x-3)^2+(y-4)^2&=9\end{align*}$$
At $x=0$:
$$\begin{align*}9+(y-4)^2&=9\\(y-4)^2&=0\\y&=4\end{align*}$$
The $y$-intercept is $(0,4)$. The lowest point has $y=4-3=1$, so there are no $x$-intercepts.

spec.description: Equal-scale coordinate axes and supplied blue circle through the origin and (0,-6). Centre lies below the x=3 tick; dashed radius joins the origin to the centre. Preserve only source ticks 3 and -6, with no grid or origin label. Source graph blue is normalised to the standard series blue.
spec.answerVisibility: Source curve, axes, centre and dashed radius remain visible; equation and additional coordinate labels are solution content only.

answer.worked:
The centre lies on $x=3$. The midpoint of the vertical chord joining $(0,0)$ and $(0,-6)$ has $y=-3$, so the centre is $(3,-3)$.
$$\begin{align*}r^2&=(3-0)^2+(-3-0)^2\\r^2&=18\end{align*}$$
Hence $(x-3)^2+(y+3)^2=18$.
At $y=0$:
$$\begin{align*}(x-3)^2+9&=18\\(x-3)^2&=9\\x&=0\text{ or }6\end{align*}$$
At $x=0$:
$$\begin{align*}9+(y+3)^2&=18\\(y+3)^2&=9\\y&=0\text{ or }-6\end{align*}$$
The intercepts are $(0,0)$, $(6,0)$ and $(0,-6)$.
